groups.text: A batch job holds a lock for one and a half seconds.
An A P I thread needs the same lock, and it has a two hundred millisecond budget.
With synchronized, the A P I thread can only wait at the door.
It can't give up after a timeout, and an interrupt doesn't reach it until it gets in.
ReentrantLock is the same room with the same rules: one owner, a release happens-before the next lock, and it's reentrant.
What it adds is controls on the door.
tryLock with a timeout waits at most two hundred milliseconds, then returns false, and the thread can answer busy.
lockInterruptibly waits too, but an interrupt gets it out at once.
Next, a buffer with room for two payments.
A monitor has one wait set, so producers and consumers sleep in the same place, and notify can wake the wrong kind.
A ReentrantLock can have one waiting room per reason, called a Condition.
Consumers wait in notEmpty.
Producers wait in notFull.
The buffer is empty.
A consumer calls await on notEmpty.
That gives back the lock, and parks it in its own room.
A second consumer does the same.
A producer takes the lock, adds a payment, and calls signal on notEmpty.
Which thread wakes up?
A consumer. Only consumers wait in that room.
It goes back to the door for the lock, then checks the buffer again in its while loop.
Last, an FX rate cache, read five thousand times a second and refreshed every five seconds.
With a plain lock, readers wait for each other for nothing.
A ReentrantReadWriteLock lets any number of readers in together.
The writer needs the room empty, so it waits until the last reader leaves.
Then it writes alone, and new readers wait.
In code, nothing lets go for you.
Call lock just before try, and release it first thing in finally.
Kotlin's withLock writes that for you.
Explicit locks keep the rules of synchronized.
They add a door you can leave, a waiting room per condition, and a read mode many threads share.
Quick check. Two consumers wait in notEmpty, and a producer waits in notFull.
A consumer takes a payment and signals notFull.
Who wakes up?
